pol_lead: The policy is the complete configuration the CI applies to every project. Developers follow the rules; only the people who administer the policy repository change them.
pol_copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.
pol_copy_command: Copy the command that opens the policy
pol_band_text: Saving changes the files of {name}, not a project.
pol_unavailable_title: This screen is not available in the policy
pol_unavailable_lead: You are editing the CI policy, which is not a project: there is no code to validate here. To validate a project, open the interface inside it with jgates ui; to see what the policy does on a project, use Test against a project.
pol_project_local: The configuration of this project is editable here. It applies to local validations.
pol_project_governed: The CI of this project is governed by the policy {policy}; the project configuration is locked.
pol_project_how: The CI rules live in a separate policy repository. To edit them with these same screens, open the interface on the policy folder:
pol_project_note: In that mode the Configuration and Tools screens save to the policy folder, and this screen shows the fingerprint and the ready CI snippets.
pol_hash_lead: The CI only runs when the policy it downloaded has exactly this fingerprint. Update the protected CI variable after each approved change.
pol_hash_rule: The value is computed on every read from the files in the folder; it changes as soon as a profile, a tool or any file of the set is saved.
pol_files_lead: Only the files JGates reads enter the fingerprint: jgates.yml, the .jgates folder and the files the configuration points to.
pol_files_caption: Files that enter the policy fingerprint
pol_ci_lead: Set these variables in the project CI and use the ready job below.
pol_var_dir: Folder where the CI downloads the policy repository, outside the project folder.
pol_ci_protect: Keep the fingerprint in a protected variable: only the people who administer the CI should be able to change it.
pol_ci_platform: Keeping the job in the pipeline is up to the platform: on GitLab, a compliance or group pipeline with a protected pipeline file; on GitHub, required workflows by ruleset and CODEOWNERS on the workflow.
pol_test_lead: Pick a project folder to see the plan jgates ci would make with this policy. Nothing is written, neither in the project nor in the policy.
pol_test_readonly: Read only: no file was changed.
pol_test_counts: {run} will run, {off} off or not applicable, {uncovered} requirements without coverage
